#Sequinned Steps - LGBT Sydney

##Tour snapshot
Sydney's world-famous Mardi Gras is the evolution of over 200 years of gay and lesbian history in this city. From the gay governor whose conduct scandalised the British Empire to the bright lights of Oxford Street, hear the stories and see the sites that make Sydney one of the friendliest cities for gay and lesbian culture in the world. Your guide brings the hidden history to life, one laneway and landmark at a time.

##Highlights
* Uncover the hidden tales of key gay and lesbian figures who shaped the Sydney landscape
* Walk Oxford Street, the traditional heart of Sydney's gay and lesbian scene
* Learn the story behind the world-famous Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras
* Finish with a drink (additional cost) at an iconic gay hangout, and you might just share a table with a drag queen

Inclusions: Local English-speaking guide, choice of alcoholic/non-alcoholic drink (additional cost) at the conclusion of the tour.
Exclusions: Additional food and drink, souvenirs and items of a personal nature, tips or gratuities for your guide.

picturesque Jiguma Track situated on Thaua Country in Pambula Beach New South Wales. Join your local

- a current Australian driver's licence (vehicle)

description: Embark on an immersive journey through the stunning landscapes of the Hauraki Coromandel Peninsula, where natural beauty meets Māori cultural heritage. Starting with a pick-up from the Matariki Tours Hub at 150 Pound Street, Coromandel, guests will set off on a scenic round-trip along the western coast of the peninsula to Colville, where they can relax and enjoy morning tea at the charming Pickled Hereford Café.

Through captivating storytelling, the kaikorero will reveal the significance of Matariki (the Māori New Year) and share the profound connection Māori culture holds with "Papatūānuku" (Mother Earth), "Ranginui" (Father Sky), and "Tikapa Moana" (the ancestral ocean).

Afterward, guests will be transported back to Coromandel Town, where they can explore local shops and enjoy the vibrant hospitality scene. This tour offers an ideal blend of adventure, cultural enrichment, and the chance to experience the charm of Coromandel’s community firsthand.

#Join us for a unique and exclusive Wellington sightseeing experience.

##Rates
Adult: $150
Child: $75

##Duration 
3.5 hours

##About 
Shenandoah, one of our favourite Wellington tours and exclusive to Xplor Tours, takes you to perhaps the best but least known destination in the region.

Approximately 20 minutes’ drive from Wellington, overlooking the sparkling Pauatahanui Inlet and linked with Battle Hill (a significant Maori War site), Shenandoah is a working farm and hidden historical gem inside a native wild birdlife reserve.

Once Xplor Tours drops you there, owner and proud Kiwi Simon takes you on a unique and magical tour around his beautiful, relaxing property, and through its history.

Originally a Maori Fortress Pa for Ngati Toa in the 1800’s, the property has seen three different owners over 150 years. After withstanding a major battle with English troops, it became a Crown Fort to guard the stagecoach road from highway robbers. Some of the first settlers to New Zealand made contact with the local iwi here, before the whalers and settlers transformed Pauatahanui into the thriving rural community of today.

Early in World War II, Shenandoah was commandeered as a US Marine training base and housed over 100,000 troops, ushering in the next military episode of the site.

The history isn’t just told in stories though; behind the barn doors, a private museum is filled with artifacts found on the property which date back over the last 150 years.

As part of your day trip to Shenandoah with Xplor Tours, you can relax by the pond and jetty or other seating areas in the gardens, and enjoy a tea or coffee with morning or afternoon tea.

Simon’s passion and ability to enthral makes this Wellington tour experience genuinely unique and one that will stay with you long after you leave Shenandoah.

Come on a Shenandoah tour with Xplor Tours and you will see why “Pauatahanui” means “the place you never want to leave from.”

##More info 
We don’t want to spoil all the surprises, but this is the Wellington tour to do if you want to experience any or all of the following:
Unique Wellington Tour of a hidden gem.
Rich in local history, from the Maori Wars through to WWII.
Collections of rare vintage examples of a certain well-known marque of American motorbikes.
Exploring formal and less formal gardens and native bush.
Seeing and interacting with farm animals, wildlife and birdlife.
Experiencing the history of an area in a living museum complete with the personal stories of the people involved.
Enjoying refreshments in a beautiful, scenic and relaxing location.

Shenandoah, one of our favourite Wellington tours and exclusive to Xplor Tours, takes you to perhaps the best but least known destination in the region.

Approximately 20 minutes’ drive from Wellington, overlooking the sparkling Pauatahanui Inlet and linked with Battle Hill (a significant Maori War site), Shenandoah is a working farm and hidden historical gem inside a native wild birdlife reserve.

Once Xplor Tours drops you there, owner and proud Kiwi Simon takes you on a unique and magical tour around his beautiful, relaxing property, and through its history.

Originally a Maori Fortress Pa for Ngati Toa in the 1800’s, the property has seen three different owners over 150 years. After withstanding a major battle with English troops, it became a Crown Fort to guard the stagecoach road from highway robbers. Early in World War II, Shenandoah was commandeered as a US Marine training base and housed over 100,000 troops, ushering in the next military episode of the site.

The history isn’t just told in stories though; behind the barn doors, a private museum is filled with artifacts found on the property which date back over the last 150 years.

Simon’s passion and ability to enthral makes this Wellington tour experience genuinely unique and one that will stay with you long after you leave Shenandoah.

Explore the stunning Freycinet National Park on this full-day adventure from Hobart. Discover the world-famous Wineglass Bay, hike to the iconic lookout for breathtaking coastal views, and enjoy time to relax on pristine white-sand beaches. Along the way, experience dramatic granite peaks, crystal-clear waters, and abundant Tasmanian wildlife. This tour combines scenic walks, beach time, and guided insights into the region’s natural history, making it the perfect escape for nature lovers seeking one of Tasmania’s most celebrated landscapes.
itinerary: DAY ONE - Arrive in the breathtaking wilderness of Tasmania and journey to the iconic Freycinet National Park—where turquoise waters meet rugged pink granite peaks.
- We’ll take care of the logistics, with optional transfers available from Launceston, so you can fully relax and step straight into adventure.
- Your journey begins with a spectacular coastal hike along Hazards Beach, where pristine white sands and crystal-clear waters set the tone for the days ahead.

- We continue on to the secluded beauty of Cooks Beach, where we’ll establish camp for the night. Along the way, enjoy a guided walk to the famous Wineglass Bay Lookout—your first glimpse of one of the world’s most iconic views.

- As the sun lowers, unwind with a refreshing swim, followed by a relaxed dinner by the beach under the Tasmanian sky.

DAY TWO - Rise early for an unforgettable climb to the summit of Mt Freycinet—rewarded with sweeping panoramic views across the peninsula and beyond.

- From here, we continue on to Mt Graham, where we’ll pause for a well-earned lunch overlooking the dramatic east coast.

- Descending towards Wineglass Bay, take time to relax on its pristine shores—swim, rest, and soak in the beauty of this truly special place.

- We then make our way back towards camp in the Wineglass Bay region for another peaceful evening. Enjoy free time to unwind, freshen up, and share a nourishing dinner with the group.

DAY THREE - On our final morning, we take on the exhilarating climb up Mt Amos—arguably the best vantage point over Wineglass Bay.

After soaking in the final views and capturing those unforgettable moments, we return to camp, pack up, and begin our journey home—leaving with a sense of achievement, connection, and lasting memories of Tasmania’s wild beauty.

itinerary: We offer a rich and immersive cultural tourism experience that invites visitors to connect deeply with the living traditions of the Northern Peninsula Area (NPA) and the Torres Strait. At the heart of this experience is traditional Torres Strait Islander dance, where powerful storytelling is expressed through movement, rhythm, and song, reflecting connection to land, sea, ancestors, and identity. The Northern Peninsula Area (NPA) is the gateway to the stunningTorres Strait Islands, known as Zenadth Kes.

Visitors will be introduced to the Kala Lagaw Ya language, one of the traditional languages of the Torres Strait, through guided storytelling sessions. These stories share knowledge of the Tagai constellation, seasonal changes, island life, and cultural values passed down through generations. This creates a meaningful opportunity for visitors to not just observe, but understand the worldview and knowledge systems of Torres Strait Islander people.

The experience is further enriched through traditional island food tasting, where guests can sample local foods such as fresh seafood, damper, coconut-based dishes, and other culturally significant ingredients. These tastings highlight the strong relationship between people, sea country, and sustainable practices.

Visitors can also purchase authentic arts and crafts, including hand-made items such as woven baskets, carvings, jewellery, and cultural artefacts created by local artists. Each piece carries cultural meaning and provides a direct way to support local creators and keep traditions strong.

Together, these elements create a holistic cultural experience that goes beyond tourism. It fosters respect, understanding, and genuine connection—allowing visitors to experience the true spirit, resilience, and cultural richness of the NPA and Torres Strait.
highlights: Guba Markay was established in 1990. It is a proud Bamaga Traditonal Dance Group, showcasing the movement, history, and cultural legacy of people who relocated from Saibai Island in the Torres Strait to Muttee Head, mainland Australia in 1947. Through our performances we honour the strength and resilence of our Elders and ancestors.

Our achievements include the Gold Winners 2020 Sydney Dance Rites, Gold Laura Festival 2018, Gold Weipa Cultural Festival 1995 and many more. We perform at festivals and deliver a full cultural experience showcasing our seven clan stories and ancestral movements.
